ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the image is a schematic diagram of the layout of China's high-speed railway "four horizontal and four vertical" passenger dedicated lines. It can be seen that many high-speed railway lines are concentrated in the eastern and central regions of China, and nodes such as Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, Harbin, Dalian, Zhengzhou, and Xi'an are marked. Among the four candidate lines, the Beijing-Shanghai line is located in the east, running from Beijing southeastward to Shanghai; the Beijing-Guangzhou line runs from Beijing further south to Guangzhou; the Harbin-Dalian line is located in the northeast, connecting the area of Harbin and Dalian; the Zhengzhou-Xi'an line is located in the central-western part, running from Zhengzhou to Xi'an. Then reason: from the perspective of natural factors, the amount of engineering work per unit length and the cost are mainly affected by terrain undulation, mountains and hills, river valley crossings, frozen soil and severe cold, etc. The Beijing-Shanghai High-Speed Railway mainly passes through the North China Plain, the low and flat Jianghuai region, and the Yangtze River Delta, with flat terrain, and relatively fewer bridges, tunnels, and large-scale earthwork and stonework projects are needed; the southern section of the Beijing-Guangzhou line passes through more hilly and mountainous areas; the Harbin-Dalian line is affected by severe cold in Northeast China, frozen soil, and some mountains and hills; the Zhengzhou-Xi'an line passes through the Loess Plateau, mountains, and river valley areas, with greater engineering difficulty. Therefore, among the four, the one with the smallest amount of engineering work per unit length and the lowest cost is the Beijing-Shanghai High-Speed Railway.

Read the schematic diagram of the layout of China's high-speed railway "four horizontal and four vertical" passenger dedicated lines. <image1>
Considering natural factors, among the four completed and opened high-speed railways of Beijing-Guangzhou, Beijing-Shanghai, Harbin-Dalian, and Zhengzhou-Xi'an, which one has the smallest amount of engineering work per unit length and the lowest cost?
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Read the schematic diagram of the layout of China's high-speed railway "four horizontal and four vertical" passenger dedicated lines. <image1> Considering natural factors, among the four completed and opened high-speed railways of Beijing-Guangzhou, Beijing-Shanghai, Harbin-Dalian, and Zhengzhou-Xi'an, which one has the smallest amount of engineering work per unit length and the lowest cost?
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the image is a schematic diagram of the layout of China's high-speed railway "four horizontal and four vertical" passenger dedicated lines. It can be seen that many high-speed railway lines are concentrated in the eastern and central regions of China, and nodes such as Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, Harbin, Dalian, Zhengzhou, and Xi'an are marked. Among the four candidate lines, the Beijing-Shanghai line is located in the east, running from Beijing southeastward to Shanghai; the Beijing-Guangzhou line runs from Beijing further south to Guangzhou; the Harbin-Dalian line is located in the northeast, connecting the area of Harbin and Dalian; the Zhengzhou-Xi'an line is located in the central-western part, running from Zhengzhou to Xi'an. Then reason: from the perspective of natural factors, the amount of engineering work per unit length and the cost are mainly affected by terrain undulation, mountains and hills, river valley crossings, frozen soil and severe cold, etc. The Beijing-Shanghai High-Speed Railway mainly passes through the North China Plain, the low and flat Jianghuai region, and the Yangtze River Delta, with flat terrain, and relatively fewer bridges, tunnels, and large-scale earthwork and stonework projects are needed; the southern section of the Beijing-Guangzhou line passes through more hilly and mountainous areas; the Harbin-Dalian line is affected by severe cold in Northeast China, frozen soil, and some mountains and hills; the Zhengzhou-Xi'an line passes through the Loess Plateau, mountains, and river valley areas, with greater engineering difficulty. Therefore, among the four, the one with the smallest amount of engineering work per unit length and the lowest cost is the Beijing-Shanghai High-Speed Railway.
